title: 1969 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Let \(n\) be the number of points \(P\) interior to the region bounded by a circle with radius \(1,\) such that the sum of the squares of the distances from \(P\) to the endpoints of a given diameter is \(3.\) Then \(n\) is:

solutions.text:
Let \(P=(x,y)\) and take the diameter endpoints as \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0).\) The condition becomes \[ \begin{aligned} PA^2+PB^2&=3,\\ 2x^2+2y^2+2&=3. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(x^2+y^2=\frac{1}{2}.\) This is an entire circle of radius \(\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\) lying inside the given unit circle. It contains infinitely many points.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Place the circle at the origin with diameter endpoints \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0)\)
Simplify the sum of the two squared distances
